title: prompt-and-tool-contract-linter-scratchpad
content:
PURPOSE
---
Personal sketch for a lightweight linter that validates: 1) prompt shape and safety heuristics, 2) tool/plugin contract manifests and schemas, and 3) CI-friendly rules for PR gating. Think: pre-commit + server API + Redwood Console integration.

MOTIVATION / PROBLEM STATEMENT
---
- We keep shipping subtle tool-contract regressions: incorrect param shapes, missing capability flags, ambiguous return schemas.
- Prompts drift: magic tokens, system instruction leakage, or unsafe instruction patterns get copied around.
- Need deterministic, fast feedback for engineers (local + CI) and optional runtime telemetry to correlate rules -> quality regressions.

HIGH-LEVEL DESIGN
---
Three components:
1) CLI linter (local, fast) - pre-commit hook friendly
2) Lint server (optional) - POST /lint for CI and Console integration
3) Rule registry + rule DSL - pluggable rules written in simple YAML/JS snippets

ASCII diagram (sketch):

 dev (pre-commit) ---> prompt-lint-cli ---> returns (ok|errors)
                              |
                              v
                       optional: POST /lint to lint-server
                              |
     Redwood Console <--- lint-server (aggregates, history, rule-metrics)

CORE CONCEPTS
---
- Input types: prompt, chat transcript, tool-manifest.json, tool-contract.proto (or simplified schema).
- Normalizer: canonicalize whitespace, normalize token placeholders ({{user}} -> <USER>), strip innocuous comments.
- Rule: predicate + message + fix (optional).
- Severity levels: error | warn | info | suggestion.
- Autofix: for trivial fixes (trim trailing spaces, replace deprecated placeholders)
- Baseline mode: allowlist existing violations per repo (baseline file), useful for incremental adoption.

SAMPLE RULE DSL (YAML-ish)
---
- id: no-system-instruction-override
  types: [prompt, chat]
  severity: error
  description: Disallow user-level system instructions that override global system message.
  predicate: "contains_regex('^\\s*(SYSTEM:|#system)')"
  fixer: null

- id: tool-params-schema-match
  types: [tool-manifest]
  severity: error
  description: Tool manifest params must declare types and example for each param
  predicate: "required_keys(['params']) and all(params, k -> has_keys(k, ['name','type','example']))"
  fixer: null

NOTE: predicate language is intentionally tiny - can be compiled to JS or run with a sandboxed evaluator.

SAMPLE TOOL-MANIFEST (common problems we check)
---
{
  "name": "calendar.add_event",
  "version": "0.3",
  "params": [
    {"name": "title", "type": "string", "example": "1:1 with Sam"},
    {"name": "start_time", "type": "iso_datetime", "example": "2024-11-12T15:00:00Z"}
  ],
  "response_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"event_id": {"type": "string"}}}
}

COMMON LINT CHECKS (starter set)
---
- Prompt checks:
  - disallow raw API keys/tokens patterns (regex + entropy heuristic)
  - system-instruction duplication across prompt and tool manifest
  - banned-instructions list (e.g., "delete account") -> warn or error depending on repo policy
  - placeholder hygiene: flag unknown {{foo}} placeholders

- Tool manifest checks:
  - params declared with name/type/example
  - response_schema present and not just "any"
  - idempotency flag present when side-effects possible
  - permission-scopes declared (list of scopes)
  - runtime-timeout hint present (ms)

- Contract checks (integration):
  - tool invocation examples parse against params schema
  - example responses match response_schema

LINT SERVER API SHAPE (sketch)
---
POST /v1/lint/run
headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
body: { "repo": "org/repo", "files": [{"path":"prompts/welcome.txt","content":"..."}], "baseline": "optional-base64" }
response: { "status":"ok", "results": [{"file":"prompts/welcome.txt","issues":[{"rule":"no-system-instruction-override","severity":"error","line":12,"message":"..."}]}], "metrics": {"error_count": 3}}

Design notes: server should be idempotent, return a short result set (first N issues) for CI. Full results link -> Console.

CI INTEGRATION PATTERNS
---
- pre-commit hook: run prompt-lint-cli on changed files, exit 1 on errors (unless --baseline).
- GitHub Action: call lint-server with changed files; annotate PR with comments for first 10 issues.
- Jenkins/Gitlab: same, use CLI for environments with no outbound access.

REDWOOD CONSOLE USAGE
---
- Expose a per-repo lint history page that aggregates rule failures and time trends.
- Correlate failures with eval regressions (if a prompt rule flags higher, show associated metric from Optimize).
- Allow rule toggles per-team (team-level policy overrides).

EXAMPLE OUTPUT FORMAT (CLI friendly)
---

prompts/welcome.txt:12:error:no-system-instruction-override: Remove the leading SYSTEM: line.
calendar/manifest.json:2:warn:response-schema-missing: Add response_schema to help with client generation.

AUTOFIX EXAMPLES
---
- Trim trailing whitespace in prompt files.
- Normalize {{ user }} -> {{user}} (consistent spacing).
- Replace deprecated placeholder %USERNAME% -> {{user}} (configurable map).

ADOPTION STRATEGY
---
Phase 0: prototype CLI with ~10 rules, run locally (1 week).
Phase 1: add GitHub Action + baseline support (2 weeks).
Phase 2: lint-server + Console integration + metrics (3-4 weeks).

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS
---
- Predicate DSL security: do we evaluate arbitrary JS? prefer a tiny declarative language compiled to a safe evaluator.
- Performance: large prompt corpora in monorepos - need file sampling or changed-file-only mode.
- Multilingual prompts: token-detection heuristics need to be language-aware.
- False positives on placeholders used for runtime substitution; need repo-specific allowlists.

NEXT ACTIONS / TODOS
---
- [Jamie] prototype CLI skeleton that reads files and applies rule YAML (today).
- [Ravi] spike on a tiny predicate evaluator in Rust (WASM target) for speed and safety (next week).
- [Sofia] draft GH Action + annotation strategy (this week).
- Create GH issue: github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-linting/issues/PR-boot

NOTES TO SELF
---
- Keep rule format minimal so non-devs (PMs, solutions) can write simple checks.
- Think about shipping as an internal package first (pip/npm) then OSS subset.
- Consider integration points with model-eval: rule -> eval set automatic generation (if rule triggers change, create small eval).

END
